title: Dedicated Capacity Concierge: Intake Funnel and SLA Prioritization Rubric
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Enterprise customers requesting dedicated GPU capacity arrive with uneven information (expected QPS, latency targets, token distribution, model family preferences) which makes SLA negotiation slow and error-prone. Goal: Define a structured intake funnel + scoring rubric that enables rapid, defensible recommendations for reserved throughput, GPU class, and scaling policy. Deliver an operator-friendly decision log and a lightweight automation that produces an initial recommendation for 90% of requests. Scope: This ticket covers the PM-side product definition, decision rubric, intake questionnaire, and handoff checklist for Eng/Support. Implementation of automation (assistant) will be a follow-up ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Clear intake questionnaire with 12 canonical fields that captures workload fingerprint (latency SLO, sustained tokens/s, peak burst, model family, KV cache characteristics, security constraints)
Scoring matrix that yields one of three SLA bands (Gold, Silver, Bronze) and recommends GPU class (H100, A100, L4) and reservation size in GPU units or token/s equivalent
Operator checklist for pre-onboarding validation and three standard fallback policies (same-region model variant, cross-region fallback, soft-degrade to batch-optimized variant)
Sample decision log template for each intake containing inputs, computed score, recommended reservation, and rationale for audit
Conservative automation prototype that produces a recommended SLA band and GPU class for 90% of historical intake forms when run offline against last 18 months of requests
intake_questionnaire: Customer name and primary contact (email + phone)
Primary workload type: chat, completions, embeddings, reranking, hybrid
Target p95 latency (ms) and acceptable tail behaviour (p99/p999)
Expected sustained tokens/s and max burst tokens/s during peak windows
Sequence length distribution: median, 90th percentile, estimated KV cache hit rate
Models of choice and acceptable model variants (quantized variants, smaller transformer families)
Data residency, VPC / on-prem requirement, encryption/KMS needs
Compliance constraints (SOC2/ISO/PCI/other) and audit log retention requirements
Tolerance for preemption or use of preemptible instances during burst
Business criticality (internal dev/test, public-facing product, regulated workload)
Planned rollout cadence and required rollout controls (canary % schedules)
Expected contract term and budget guardrails
scoring_matrix: Weighting overview: Latency SLO 35%, Sustained throughput 25%, Peak burst 15%, Model affinity 10%, Security/compliance 10%, Business criticality 5%
Gold band: p95 <= 150ms OR sustained tokens/s > threshold mapped to X GPU units; reserved non-preemptible; recommended GPUs: H100 or high-memory A100 depending on KV cache needs
Silver band: p95 <= 350ms and moderate sustained throughput; allow scheduled burst credits; recommended GPUs: A100 or mixed pool
Bronze band: best-effort latency or batch-friendly workloads; recommend cost-optimized L4/quantized variants with elastic scaling and preemptible burst
GPU affinity rules: KV-heavy workloads prefer higher-memory A100; smaller models and quantized pipelines prefer L4; very low-latency transformer engines prefer H100
Budget guardrail: automatically suggest a lower-tier band when customer budget < computed expected monthly cost unless customer signs for commitment
decision_guidelines: When a customer specifies strict p95 and high sustained tokens/s, prefer Gold with reserved capacity and explicit node-pinning; require Security & Infra signoff for on-prem/VPC
If customer requests strict latency but is flexible on cost, propose model variant with lower memory footprint and higher attention kernel (runtime-led optimization) and recommend H100
If KV cache hit-rate < 20% and sequence lengths are long, recommend larger memory GPU and provision extra KV cache capacity
For customers with regulatory constraints, include audit log retention and KMS integration in the SLA and elevate to Silver+ by default
Default burst policy: 10% sustained buffer with eligible burst credits up to 2x declared peak for 10 minutes; escalate to Concierge review for exceptions
Fallback policy ordering: 1) model variant with same architecture and lower GPU footprint 2) cross-region fallback to same tier 3) degrade to batch-optimized route with user-visible rate limiting
notes: Trade-off: aggressive automatic recommendations reduce cycle time but increase risk of overprovisioning. Plan conservative defaults and explicit opt-in for aggressive autosize.
Partial decision: agreed to three SLA bands instead of 5 to keep operator mental model simple; follow-up can expand bands if demand requires.
Technical implication: automation needs historical request fingerprinting + cost model that maps tokens/s to GPU units. Runtime team to estimate conversion heuristics.
Operational: require a 'concierge review' checkbox for any Gold recommendation that exceeds $Xk monthly spend.
Risk: Customers may under-report burst; include a mandatory example traffic trace or synthetic test before finalizing reservation.
